# Feature matrix

<!-- Generated from engine/traceability/feature-matrix.json by `npm run check:traceability` in engine/ (write mode: `node scripts/gen-feature-matrix.mjs`). Do not edit by hand. -->

What the engine implements, each row with its evidence. Generated from
[`engine/traceability/feature-matrix.json`](../../engine/traceability/feature-matrix.json) by
`engine/scripts/gen-feature-matrix.mjs`; CI runs it with `--check` (`npm run check:traceability`), which
fails when an evidence path does not exist, a rule below is broken, or this file is not the render. Do not
edit this file by hand: change the JSON and run `node scripts/gen-feature-matrix.mjs` in `engine/`.

Engine column:

- **wired**: reachable from the runtime or host path, and proved by at least one engine test.
- **partial**: the core exists and is unit-tested, but key behaviour is not wired.
- **contract only**: exported and unit-tested, never invoked outside tests.

Every non-PDF subsystem is enforced in CI (`npm run ci` and `npm run gates` in `engine/`).

A rule is a **formula**, text in a FEEL subset (`age(dateOfBirth) >= 18`, `if … then … else …`, `today()`; [docs/formulas.md](../formulas.md)), an expression tree, or `{ formula, run }` where `run` is `both`, `browser`, `server` or `server-secret`. Each runtime compiles a copy of the definition and never changes the author's object. A formula that does not parse is an absent rule, said or refused by the `formulaErrors` policy (`warn`, `fail`). |

Answers print as text, so long values wrap. The root's `configuration.print` sets the versions offered and the default, a first-page heading, the print scale, journey page breaks and a running header and footer as two lines of text each with `{{placeholders}}` (title, date, page counters, `receipt.` from the notice's `data`, `host.`, a field's value path), edited in the builder's Print workspace; each component chooses in the inspector's On paper group where it is drawn (both, screen only, paper only), whether it starts a new page or stays whole, and whether it prints while a rule hides it (as on screen, always, only when answered), and a live form and a read-only form print differently. It uses CSS page-margin boxes (Chromium) and `zoom`. A cancelable `datum-print` event hands the document to a host that routes it elsewhere. What a print theme can and cannot restyle on paper is in [`docs/print-support.md`](../print-support.md). The PDF pipeline is separate: real bytes from the kernel, not the browser's print dialog. |

Timing attributes: `data-source-wait` (`none`, the default, paints the form at once with a loading note under each field whose choices are coming; `all` shows "Loading form…" until every source has answered or timed out), `data-source-timeout` (milliseconds a data source may take, 15000 by default, `0` for no limit; a source over it has failed) and `wasm-timeout` (milliseconds the sandbox module may take to load, 15000 by default, `0` for no limit; a submit after it is refused as validator unavailable); a loaded `datum-wasm.js` is refused when its exported `WASM_ABI_VERSION` is not the element's own. [`docs/data-sources.md`](../data-sources.md) has the data-source side. |

The docs site's builder examples use contained. |

`packages/pdf-kernel` is that provider: one TypeScript program run in-process or inside the QuickJS-WASM sandbox, byte-identical either way, with embedded fonts, tagging and template fill/inspect. Layouts are named `pdf.layouts[]` on the definition (several per form, custom or populating an existing PDF), designed through the ordinary builder as its PDF mode (`createPdfBuilderMode`, loaded lazily by `<datum-form-builder>`; the bundle exports `loadPdfBuilderMode()` / `loadJourneyBuilderMode()` instead of the factories); no layout derives one from the form. A layout may carry a `when`: a download that names none prints the first whose condition holds on the answers, else the default, alike in the browser, the program and the submissions server. The renderer carries no PDF layer until a host asks for one. Guide: [`docs/pdf-rendering.md`](../pdf-rendering.md). |

The docs site's Signing page shows it in a live example. |

## Not yet wired

What remains, all deliberate:

| Deferred | Why |
|---|---|
| Further signing work | PDFs are signed by the server with its own certificate or by the person with the certificate on their YubiKey or in a certificate file through the local agent, and submissions with the person's passkey; the Spring Boot and Node hosts verify passkey-signed submissions. Left: long-term validation material (a DSS with OCSP/CRL; the kernel only classifies one on verify), packaged agent binaries (the agent runs from `pip install`), passkey verification in the FastAPI host, and a WebAuthn signature on the PDF itself. |
| Authoring `collection` in the builder | A data grid is the one collection the builder makes: its binding is set at its id and the inspector edits `minRows` / `maxRows`. Any other repeating container has no editor, and the JSON tab shows `collection` but refuses to change it. |
